newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices mostly sink with crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices mostly sink with crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices mostly lost ground Wednesday in sluggish activity, with sinking crude prices and relatively mild East Coast weather pressuring the complex, industry sources said.
"There's plenty of oil around, particularly high sulphur, and there hasn't been a lot of demand," said one cash trader, noting increased HS supply from Venezuela recently.

In New York Harbor, high sulphurs lost the most ground, with 2.2 percent tumbling more than 75 cents a barrel to about the $19 level, while three percent was 25-50 cents lower at about $17.50, traders said.
Traders said recent refinery problems like Star's damaged H-oil unit in Louisiana continued to pressure HSFO.
NYH physical one percent slipped a quarter to about $22.25. Traders said January one percent paper, which sold early at $21.50, was quoted later at $21.00-21.10, down about $1 on the day with crude.
At the U.S. Gulf Coast, one percent skidded 50-75 cents to about $19, while three percent notionally was off slightly to $16, traders said.
New York city gate swing gas prices were little changed Wednesday in the $4.05-4.10/mmBtu area compared to NYH one percent resid at a $3.53/mmBtu equivalent.
